extraction.Name: Samuel Horse Chief
extraction.Recorded patent: Was it filed for record? no — 61391
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold to Mr. Jefferies for $2500 cash
extraction.Occupation/Income: No interest in any inherited land. Shares in Pawnee annuity. No property or money accumulated.
extraction.NOTES: Four minor children dependent on allottee for support. $2500 which allottee considers good price at that time. Patent delivered 1918, Agency office; receipted for yes. This case should be looked into further as to actual value of the land at the time it was sold. Document also contains a separate record for Eva N. Duncan, Allotment No. 251, whose S/2 was sold to Frank Armstrong for $3500 and N/2 has mortgage of $850 due in 1931; she has eight minor children; fee patent date Dec. 6, 1917; delivered Jan. 24, 1918; age 43, good health; income $100 per year from inherited land and share in Pawnee annuity; forced to sell on account of her home burning; purchaser paid $3200 for S/2 and gave allottee a Dodge truck valued at $800. Notarized November 26, 1928; commission expires Jan. 31, 1929.
